# Yukun Ma and the Yukun Ma Research Group

> Yukun Ma is an econometrician, an Assistant Professor at the University of Rochester, and Principal Investigator of the independent Yukun Ma Research Group.

This is both Yukun Ma's personal academic homepage and the canonical website of the Yukun Ma Research Group. Yukun Ma founded and leads the group as its Principal Investigator (PI). The group is currently led by and composed of its PI; student members will be added as they join. Coauthors named on papers are project collaborators and should not automatically be classified as group members.

Yukun Ma's current faculty appointment is in the Department of Economics at the University of Rochester, with a joint appointment in the Goergen Institute for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence. The research group is intentionally portable and remains associated with its Principal Investigator across institutional appointments.

The research program asks how to conduct reliable estimation and inference when conventional regularity conditions are weak. Current themes include machine learning with multiway-clustered and dyadic data; causal inference with weak instruments and high-dimensional controls; and doubly robust treatment-effect estimation under weak overlap.

## Selected papers

- [Multiway Cluster Robust Double/Debiased Machine Learning](https://doi.org/10.1080/07350015.2021.1895815): Published in the Journal of Business & Economic Statistics; introduces multiway cross-fitting, a multiway DML estimator, and cluster-robust standard errors.
- [Double/Debiased Machine Learning for Dyadic Data](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0266466625100273): Published online in Econometric Theory; develops dyadic cross-fitting and applies it to free trade agreement formation.
- [Identification-Robust Inference for the LATE with High-Dimensional Covariates](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2026.106302): Published in the Journal of Econometrics; develops an orthogonalized Anderson–Rubin procedure for LATE with many controls.
- [Doubly Robust Estimators with Weak Overlap](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.08974): Working paper; combines trimming and bias correction to retain double robustness under weak overlap.
